answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may vote on jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by locked value and releases the stake only after a dispute window, so spawning thousands of names adds no weight unless the attacker also acquires and immobilizes substantial capital. That capital has an opportunity cost and may be slashed for proven fraud. A terrace, knoll, or hollow of empty accounts therefore cannot cheaply outweigh funded participants.
